motion.name: screen-dim
motion.purpose: Unlit screens dim (0.38) and desaturate (0.4) as the visitor scrolls; off under 60rem; no transition under reduced motion.

motion.name: step-fresh
motion.purpose: A step just written flashes the accent at 22% behind it in the file and fades; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: switch-knob
motion.purpose: The menu switch's knob slides and lights as the switch turns on; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: key-press
motion.purpose: A hint's key cap dips 2px and lights in the accent when the shortcut runs; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: tip-in
motion.purpose: A new loading-screen tip fades in from a 3px blur; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: smooth-scroll
motion.purpose: Section jumps from the nav and hint strip, only without reduced motion.

motion.name: lamp
motion.purpose: The window's RECORDING lamp breathes Save's amber glow (a drop shadow from 3px to 7px) while it runs; its count rises in over 320ms as each step lands; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: strip-away
motion.purpose: The page's hint strip slides down and fades while the window is on screen, since the window carries its own; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: invite
motion.purpose: The FLIP THIS chip arrives 700ms after the page and nudges toward its switch three times; it fades out over 320ms once the visitor touches the window; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: try-nudge
motion.purpose: TRY IT's arrow nudges 0.3rem toward the window three times, a second after the page loads; none under reduced motion.

narrative.northStar: The Game's Own Menus, Set Larger
narrative.overview:
The site is the app's world, the one recorded in the repository's root `DESIGN.md`, set larger for a page that has to persuade. It is a sibling of Hermaeus's site and keeps that site's token set role for role: the same smoked-glass ground, ink, two strengths of hairline, verdigris and frost blue accent, 3px corners, the diamond, and the same two typefaces. From the app it adds the meanings MCM Lexicon needs: DM Mono for anything matched character for character, the File Markup colors, copper on a value that differs from the mod's default, the smoked field, and the small amber diamond on a step not saved yet. A visitor who downloads MCM Lexicon opens a program that looks like the page they just left.

The first viewport is a working menu, not a pitch. The offer runs across the top: the name at display size and the hook at left, and one line of support, the Windows download, and the fine print at right behind a strong hairline. Under it, full width, sits a slice of WeaponThrowVR's real menu, drawn the way MCM Lexicon draws it, beside the step file it writes; every value set in the menu lands in the file, live, spelled as the mod spells it. The rest of the page follows Hermaeus's site: why it exists with "By the way…" asides, real screens with sticky captions and the one in view lit, the app's item table, the safety rules under hairlines, and one download row. The game's button-hint strip runs along the bottom, and every hint is a working shortcut. The docs use the same top bar and footer, with the pages listed down the left the way the app lists a menu's pages.

Where the site departs from the app: a longer type scale (display, headline, and lead are site-only), a 1rem body instead of 15px, larger buttons, a section rhythm with no app equivalent, full-width sections instead of the app's shell, a working menu as the hero, framed screens with scroll dimming, and the diamond widened from "the selected row" to "the selected thing". Inside the hero's menu, the app's own scale returns: 15px option labels, the smoked field, and the game's two-column grid, because that part is the app.
keyCharacteristics: The app's smoked-glass ground and token set, unchanged, in both themes.
A real menu, working, as the hero, writing the exact step file beside it.
Larger steps: a 6rem name and 3.75rem section titles; the app's own scale inside the menu.
One section rhythm: a caps title, a muted lead, then the material, with large gaps between sections.
Hairlines, not cards: no section, screen, or row is a filled tile, and nothing lifts on a shadow.
The bottom hint strip, D, S, and N, each a real shortcut.

rules.name: The Same Token Set Rule
rules.body: The site doesn't define colors of its own. A color the site needs is a role the app already has, with the app's dark and light values; a new role ships in both, as a pair, or not at all.

rules.name: The Changed Rule
rules.body: Copper means the player set this, and it differs from the mod's own default. It marks the value itself, never a row, a fill, or a highlight, and never doubles as a warning.

rules.name: The Draft Diamond Rule
rules.body: Amber on the site is the app's amber: the small diamond on a step not saved yet, and the read-only state. It is never decoration and never a fill.

rules.name: The Scarce Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent marks what's selected, what's actionable, and group headings inside a list. The largest accent fill is the primary download button. One exception, inherited from Hermaeus's site: the hook's promise is set in the accent, as text and never as a fill.

rules.name: The Label Versus Read Rule
rules.body: As in the app: anything that labels is tracked condensed caps; anything that's read is Jost in sentence case. A note inside a button (such as "64-bit") switches back to Jost at 0.8125rem with no tracking; a page count beside a caps page name is Jost figures.

rules.name: The File Font Rule
rules.body: DM Mono is for what MCM Recorder matches exactly: the step file, its path, and a selector. Only color sets a file's parts apart, never weight.

rules.name: The Section Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Every section after the hero is the same: the largest spacing step above it (5 to 9rem), a caps headline with a muted lead under it (up to 52rem wide), a 4rem gap, then the material. Sections don't get backgrounds or borders of their own to set them apart; the rhythm does that.

rules.name: The Scroll Inside Rule
rules.body: The demo's menu, page list, and file scroll inside themselves, never the page: the selected option starts in view on a whole row, a written step scrolls the file to it, and the options don't pass their scroll on to the page.

rules.name: The No Lift Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the page floats, so nothing has a drop shadow. Emphasis comes from light (the lit screen), the accent, the haze, and the diamond. The selected option's 1px accent outline is drawn inside its row and is a line, not a lift.

rules.name: The Real Menu Rule
rules.body: The hero's menu is WeaponThrowVR's, as MCM Lexicon reads it from the Synergy list, shown with Shizof's permission and credited in its header. Its pages, options, positions, help, ranges, and defaults are the catalog's; its labels are spelled as the mod spells them. Nothing in it is invented.

rules.name: The File Markup Rule
rules.body: As in the app: keys in the accent, since they're the words MCM Recorder reads; values in ink, since they're what it fills in; punctuation muted.

dos: **Do** use the app's tokens role for role, in both themes, and add a new color only as a dark and light pair.
**Do** give every section the same rhythm: the largest spacing step above it, a caps headline and muted lead, then the material.
**Do** show the real thing: the real menu from the catalog, real screens in hairline frames in both themes, and the exact file MCM Lexicon writes, with provenance lines for where they came from.
**Do** put the diamond on the selected thing, and only there; amber diamonds only on steps not saved yet.
**Do** set anything MCM Recorder matches exactly (step files, paths, selectors) in DM Mono, with keys in the accent, values in ink, and punctuation muted.
**Do** keep the demo's scrolling inside the demo; it never scrolls the page.
**Do** back every hint in the strip with a working shortcut, and hide the strip where there's no keyboard.
donts: **Don't** use cards, filled tiles, or section backgrounds; separate with hairlines and the section rhythm. Pane Glass is for the file, the info area, asides, and code blocks.
**Don't** put a drop shadow on anything, screens included.
**Don't** use copper anywhere the app wouldn't, or as a highlight; it marks a value that differs from the mod's default.
**Don't** add a second accent, or use the accent for decoration.
**Don't** invent or tidy a menu's labels in the demo; they're spelled as the mod spells them.
